title: Understanding the Development of Gambling Behavior in Emerging Adulthood in Türkiye: A Phenomenological Study
abstract: Gambling has increasingly become a widespread risky activity among emerging adults, accelerated by online platforms. This study explores the experiences of emerging adults in Türkiye with gambling problems and its impact on their lives. Utilizing a phenomenological design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews conducted in 2025 with 14 participants aged 19–29, recruited via social media and university announcements. Thematic analysis revealed three main themes: ‘First Contact’, ‘The Allure of Gambling’, and ‘Losses’. Results indicated that while gambling typically began with a financial motivation, it ultimately led to a loss of control alongside significant financial, psychological, and social losses. Given the limited research in Türkiye, these findings highlight an urgent need for protective policies and targeted interventions, offering valuable guidance for preventive efforts and mental health services for emerging adults.
